neighbours.label: contemplative practice instructions: directing attention inward to the breath, the body or the present moment in meditation and mindfulness; the same instruction syntax aimed at ordinary tasks stays low
fire: Lie on the mat, let your shoulders soften, and bring your awareness to your breathing.
Notice each thought as it arises, then let it go and come back to the breath.
Mindful walking means feeling each step and the contact of the feet with the ground.
With every exhale, let the tension leave your body and rest in stillness.
In this meditation you slowly scan the body from the crown of the head to the toes.
If you get distracted, simply bring your mind back to the sensation of breathing.
Sitting in silence, the monk rested his attention on the rise and fall of the belly.
Breathe in slowly, hold for a moment, and observe the stillness inside you.
quiet: Lie on the mat, lift your shoulders, and do twenty sit-ups at a steady pace.
Notice each typo as it appears, then fix it and come back to the paragraph.
Brisk walking means taking long steps and swinging your arms as you go.
With every push, lift the weight higher and lock your elbows at the top.
In this inspection you slowly check the car from the hood to the rear bumper.
If you get distracted, simply bring your eyes back to the line you were reading.
Sitting in the office, the clerk kept his attention on the stack of invoices.
Pour in the flour slowly, stir for a moment, and check the dough for lumps.
